documents: Passport plus second ID, proof of foreign address, bank reference letter, proof of income and source-of-funds documentation; banks may ask for a Grenada visa or residence.
min_deposit_fees: Not published by banks; guides cite opening deposits from zero to about USD 10,000.
banks: Republic Bank (Grenada), ACB Grenada, CIBC FirstCaribbean, Grenada Co-operative Bank (case-by-case for non-residents).
restrictions: Banks generally decline short-stay tourists; enhanced KYC, FATCA/CRS reporting and Caribbean correspondent-bank de-risking limit non-resident onboarding.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for multi-currency needs; Grenada citizenship-by-investment holders get easier access.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, bank reference, proof of income and source of wealth, CRS/FATCA self-certification; onboarding by video call and email.
min_deposit_fees: Guides cite minimum deposits around USD 1,000-5,000; fees not published.
banks: Offshore/international banks such as Belize Bank International and Heritage International Bank accept non-residents; domestic banks vary.
restrictions: Offshore (international) banks hold foreign-currency accounts only; domestic BZD accounts usually need residency; strict source-of-funds checks and CRS reporting.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut for everyday use.

documents: Passport (at least 6 months validity); most banks want a Carné de Extranjería, Peruvian address proof (rental contract, utility bill) and local phone.
min_deposit_fees: Not published for non-residents; basic accounts typically have no minimum deposit.
banks: BCP, Interbank, BBVA Peru, Scotiabank Peru (mostly residents; passport-only basic accounts case-by-case).
restrictions: Most banks require residency in practice; a 2025 SBS rule reportedly allows passport-only basic accounts but with limits; physical presence needed.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; local wallets Yape/Plin need a Peruvian bank account.

documents: Passport (notarised, apostilled copy for remote opening), proof of foreign address, bank reference letter, photo; in-branch opening needs passport only at many banks.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: Golomt Bank (remote savings account for people abroad), Khan Bank, TDB (Trade and Development Bank), XacBank (in-branch).
restrictions: No legal bar on non-residents; remote opening limited to specific products and slow; FATF grey-list exit in 2023 but enhanced due diligence remains.
alternatives: Wise for MNT transfers; QPay/SocialPay need a local account.

documents: Passport with valid visa; KITAS/KITAP, local address, NPWP tax number and Indonesian phone usually required for full accounts.
min_deposit_fees: Tourist-type accounts reportedly require USD 2,000-50,000 balance with higher fees under USD 10,000; otherwise not published.
banks: BCA, Bank Mandiri, BNI, BRI, CIMB Niaga (passport-only accounts case-by-case at branches).
restrictions: Without KITAS most banks refuse; tourist accounts are savings-only with limits; remote opening from abroad not permitted.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; Jenius/digital banks need KTP or KITAS.

documents: Passport, visa grant and expected arrival date for migrant accounts; ID verified in branch after arrival; TFN recommended (founder's home country, so this is the inbound-migrant view).
min_deposit_fees: Everyday accounts generally have no minimum deposit and no monthly fee for new migrants; interest without TFN taxed at 47%.
banks: Commonwealth Bank (apply up to 14 days pre-arrival), Westpac (up to 12 months), ANZ; NAB generally in-branch.
restrictions: Pre-arrival accounts are deposit-only until in-person ID check in Australia; non-visa-holding non-residents without arrival plans generally cannot open everyday accounts.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut Australia offer AUD details; founder's home country, so domestic accounts already available.

documents: No published non-resident process; CBA accounts opened via e-form for Nauruans and residents.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (in-country service since August 2025, replacing the Bendigo Bank agency); no domestic bank.
restrictions: Nauru uses AUD and has no locally licensed bank; CBA service targets Nauruan residents; realistic option for non-residents is an Australian account.
alternatives: An Australian bank account (AUD is legal tender); Wise.

documents: Passport, temporary registration (hotel or passport office), PINFL personal ID number, Uzbek mobile number; some banks ask non-resident questionnaire and source of funds.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; cards often free or low cost.
banks: TBC Bank Uzbekistan (app plus courier in Tashkent), Ipak Yo'li Bank, KDB Bank Uzbekistan, Asia Alliance Bank, Kapitalbank.
restrictions: Must be physically in Uzbekistan with temporary registration; currency conversion controls largely liberalised but non-resident account rules apply.
alternatives: Wise to UZS cards; local wallets Payme/Click once a card is held.

documents: Passport with visa, proof of address (foreign and often local host attestation), completed opening forms including FATCA/CRS self-certification; residence card often requested.
min_deposit_fees: No opening fee typically, but banks require a minimum balance; amounts not published.
banks: Rawbank, Equity BCDC, Ecobank RDC, Access Bank RDC, TMB (in-branch identity check required).
restrictions: Economy heavily dollarised (USD and CDF accounts); conflict in the east, enhanced AML scrutiny (FATF grey list) and correspondent de-risking; no remote opening for non-residents found.
alternatives: Mobile money (M-Pesa Vodacom, Orange Money, Airtel Money) with local SIM and ID; Wise does not pay out locally.

documents: Passport, proof of address, proof of source of funds, sometimes a professional reference letter; residence permit if applicable.
min_deposit_fees: Reportedly around KMF 10,000 for some local accounts; otherwise not published.
banks: BIC Comores (Banque pour l'Industrie et le Commerce), Exim Bank Comores, Banque de Développement des Comores (case-by-case, in person).
restrictions: Small cash-based banking system with scarce ATMs; KMF pegged to the euro under French Treasury arrangement; no published non-resident process.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut held abroad; local mobile money requires a Comorian SIM and ID.

documents: Passport, proof of local residence, residence or work permit, tax number; in-branch verification.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: None known for non-residents; Standard Bank Eswatini, FNB Eswatini, Nedbank Eswatini and Eswatini Bank serve residents and permit holders.
restrictions: Common Monetary Area exchange controls classify non-CMA persons as non-residents; banks require permits; practical workaround is a South African non-resident account usable across the CMA.
alternatives: Standard Bank South Africa non-resident account (opened remotely, ZAR usable in Eswatini); Wise; MTN MoMo with local SIM.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, foreign tax ID (CRS), source-of-wealth and income evidence; video identification accepted by Swiss regulation.
min_deposit_fees: Swissquote reportedly requires a first deposit of about CHF/EUR 500; private banks often require CHF 100,000+; non-resident account fees generally higher.
banks: Swissquote and Dukascopy Bank (remote onboarding for many countries); UBS and cantonal/private banks for higher-balance clients.
restrictions: No banking secrecy for tax (CRS/AEOI with Australia); many retail banks refuse foreign domiciles or US persons; bank-specific excluded-country lists.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; Yuh and Neon are limited to Swiss/EU residents.

documents: Passport, Slovenian tax number (davčna številka, obtained via form DR-02 from FURS, by mail or in person), foreign tax number and proof of foreign address.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; standard account fees typically a few euros per month.
banks: NLB, OTP banka, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank (Slovenia), Addiko Bank, Sparkasse (branch opening).
restrictions: Some banks cap deposits/withdrawals on non-resident accounts; EU AML and CRS reporting apply; online opening generally needs Slovenian e-ID.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, N26 (EU IBANs, for EEA residents).

documents: Passport with notarised Russian or Belarusian translation, proof of legal stay (visa/registration) at some banks, local phone number for SMS codes.
min_deposit_fees: Reported large frozen minimum balances for non-resident foreign-currency accounts at some banks (e.g. Priorbank); not officially published.
banks: Priorbank, Belarusbank, Belagroprombank (in person or via notarised power of attorney).
restrictions: Currency law allows non-resident accounts but banks may refuse; Australian, EU and US sanctions on Belarus and several state banks; restricted SWIFT and foreign-card access.
alternatives: None practical for an Australian; Wise and Revolut do not support BYN.

documents: Passport, D-number or Norwegian national ID number (needed for BankID), proof of foreign address and purpose; some banks order a D-number for the client.
min_deposit_fees: Non-resident accounts often require a large deposit; amounts not published.
banks: Some SpareBank 1 banks and local savings banks case-by-case; DNB reportedly stopped non-resident onboarding.
restrictions: Without a D-number access is often savings-only; BankID needed for online banking; strict AML/CRS checks.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut; Vipps requires a Norwegian bank account.

documents: Passport, codice fiscale (free from Agenzia delle Entrate or an Italian consulate abroad), proof of foreign address and foreign tax ID.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; conto non residenti fees vary by bank, often a monthly fee plus imposta di bollo.
banks: Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, BNL BNP Paribas, Banco BPM (conto corrente non residenti, branch visit typically required).
restrictions: Non-resident accounts may have limited services; EU AML and CRS reporting; requirements vary between branches.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, N26 (EU IBANs, for EEA residents).

documents: Passport, entry visa, recent bank statements, source of wealth declaration; most banks require a Qatar ID (QID) and salary certificate.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: QNB (non-resident accounts by direct enquiry), other banks case-by-case.
restrictions: Standard retail accounts are tied to the QID; reported pre-arrival accounts require a QID within 90 days under QCB rules.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign residence; banks may ask for further KYC.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; press reports cite DZD 50,000 deposits at some banks for clients without salary domiciliation.
banks: Not published; state banks (e.g. BNA, CPA, BEA) and foreign-owned banks such as Société Générale Algérie and BNP Paribas El Djazair offer foreign-currency accounts.
restrictions: Bank of Algeria Regulation 09-01 allows non-resident foreigners to hold foreign-currency accounts; strict exchange controls, dinar non-convertible, official rate only.
alternatives: None practical locally; Wise does not pay out in DZD.

documents: Passport or other ID approved by the Central Bank of Somaliland, physical address, source of funds and purpose of account declaration.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: Dahabshil Bank International, Premier Bank, IBS Bank (products mainly target residents and Somali diaspora).
restrictions: Unrecognised territory with limited correspondent banking and heavy de-risking; economy runs largely on USD mobile money; no published non-resident foreigner process.
alternatives: Zaad mobile money (Telesom) and eDahab with local SIM; Dahabshiil money transfer.

documents: Foreign nationals must reside in Bhutan long-term (with work permit) for a foreign currency account; remote Remit Bhutan route is for non-resident Bhutanese only.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: None known; Bank of Bhutan and Bhutan National Bank serve residents and Bhutanese nationals.
restrictions: Royal Monetary Authority circular (2012) barred banks from opening deposit accounts for non-resident foreigners; tourist payments go through licensed tour operators.
alternatives: None; pay via tour operator or international cards.

documents: Passport, Malian residence certificate and in-branch opening.
min_deposit_fees: Not published.
banks: None known for non-residents; BDM (Banque de Développement du Mali) and Ecobank Mali serve residents.
restrictions: UEMOA exchange control (BCEAO instruction 09/07/2025/RFE on non-resident accounts effective August 2025); security crisis and travel warnings make in-person opening impractical.
alternatives: Orange Money Mali or Moov Money with local SIM and ID; Wise does not support Mali payouts.

documents: Passport, valid visa or proof of legal entry, migration card, Russian phone number; INN sometimes requested.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; MIR debit cards typically free to issue.
banks: T-Bank (formerly Tinkoff) issues accounts and MIR cards to any foreigner legally present; Sberbank and others case-by-case.
restrictions: Australia is an unfriendly state: Central Bank restrictions on transfers abroad, Western sanctions on major banks (including Australian sanctions), no Visa/Mastercard international use; dealing may breach Australian sanctions law.
alternatives: None from abroad; Wise and Revolut do not support RUB transfers.
